question.text: Under the Income Tax Act, registration under Section 12AB (replacing the erstwhile 12AA) for a charitable trust such as `Vatsalya Charitable Society` is granted for a period of:

answer.text: Perpetual, subject to annual filing only
1 year, renewed annually by the Commissioner

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Section 12AB (w.e.f. 1 April 2021) provides provisional registration for 3 years for new applicants and regular registration for 5 years for existing / renewing trusts. Both are renewable on application at least 6 months before expiry. **The Trap:** Perpetual registration was the old 12AA regime — not current 12AB. 10-year non-renewable contradicts the statute. 1-year annual renewal is wrong — the regime moved from perpetual to 5-year blocks, not annual. **Cross-Exam Context:** V-A / X-A (MF Distributor / IA) test 80G donor side; XXIII tests 12AB SE-side registration. The 5-year block also applies to 80G re-validation under the same 2020 amendment — a common link point. **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** When your SE engagement starts, ask for the 12AB provisional OR regular registration certificate and note the expiry date. If within 12 months of expiry, flag a 'pending renewal' point in your management representation letter — lapsed 12AB causes taxability of the entire corpus.
